full_judgment:
This Rule arises out of the judgment and order dated 11-9-1990 passed by the learned District Judge Comilla in Miscellaneous Appeal No.34 of 1990 reversing those dated 25-3-90 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Nangalkot in Miscellaneous Case No. 29 of 1986 for pre-emption under section 96 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1951. 

 3. The pre-emptee petitioner contested the said proceeding by filing written statement and denied all the material allegations. His case was that the suit is not maintainable, the pre-emptors are not the co-sharers of case land and they had knowledge of the transfer case, that after purchase he spent about Taka 30,000.00 for the improvement of land by throwing earth to make it fit for living there. The learned Assistant Judge by his order dated 17-6-87 allowed the said case and awarded a cost of Taka 30,000.00 to be paid to the pre-emptee petitioner for the costs of improvement within 30 days otherwise the pre-emption case shall be treated as dismissed. Against the said decision the pre-emptor opposite parties preferred appeal and the appellate Court though found that some improvements have been made but he sent the case to the trial Court by his order dated 26-8-89 for fresh trial only to determine the basis of improvement cost giving opportunity to the parties to adduce evidence for such determination. 

 6. Mr. Alimuzzaman Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the pre-emptor opposite parties Nos. 1 and 2 filed counter affidavit. His submission was that whatever the petitioner did was to change the nature of the case and the same cannot come within the meaning of the improvement as enumerated in section 96(3)(b) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and it was an attempt to frustrate the pre-emption by the co-sharer opposite parties. The learned lower appellate Court committed no illegality and the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 8. Mr. Dutta has rightly submitted that the finding for determination of improvement cost is a question of fact. It appears that the trial Court decided the basis of the improvement cost in view of materials on record quite properly after remand. Now on perusal of the impugned order of the appellate Court I find it does not reflect as to how he considered the materials on record while reversing and controverting the finding of the trial Court with cogent reasons. The lower appellate Court as a final Court of fact ought to have come to his own independent finding but he has not done so and it speaks of a total non-application of his judicial mind and the same cannot be sustained in law. It appears from the record that improvement cost as made out by the petitioner was considered twice by the trial Courts earlier and the same was concurrently found by the previous appellate Court also but sent the case on remand to ascertain the basis and the trial Court on remand considered the materials for the basis of the improvement cost but the lower appellate Court passed the impugned order on mere surmise and conjecture and thereby committed serious error of law in not properly assessing and considering the materials on record and thus it suffers from legal infirmity. For the reasons stated above I find merit in the Rule.
